R28: TPS conversion only (manual cars): protected 5 V to 1N for a 0-5 V sensor on the stock plug. Never with the stock throttle switch: it shorts 1N to ground at idle; R30: TPS conversion only (manual cars): 2L to the TPS input, in place of R29. Never on an automatic: its sensor is on 2M

Fit (4.7k 0603, LCSC C23162: 48 mW at 15 V with the switch closed) only if your car's signal switches to ground or is open collector; a switch that drives 12 V must not have it; R27: 5 V pull-up for the stock throttle switch contact on 2L (manual cars, R29 fitted). Fit (4.7k 0603, LCSC C23162; 1.1 mA with the switch closed) to read the stock switch; never with a sensor on 2L

Item: Throttle position sensor, Kia, 3-pin Mazda-style plug
Notes: Also sold as 0K24718911, 0K30A18911 or aftermarket TH291 / 5S5504 / TPS4185 (rusEFI wiki list). Plugs into the car's stock throttle switch plug: 1N gives it 5 V (fit R28), 2D is its ground, 2L its signal (move R29 to R30). Before fitting R28, check with an ohmmeter which sensor pins are the track ends (constant resistance between them at any throttle) and that they meet the 1N and 2D wires; the third pin, the wiper, must meet 2L. If the reading falls as the throttle opens, TunerStudio's calibration handles it
